production.note: US model years. BMW NA's M5 history heads the car "1991 – 1993 E34 M5" and says it "arrived in the US in 1990" (calendar year). Hagerty: "1,678 coming to the USA and Canada between model years 1991 to 1993" (hagerty-1991-m5). European cars continued to 1995 with the 3.8-litre engine.

body.note: BMW NA: "the 3,804 lb. sedan". The Touring (wagon) was not sold in the US.

displacementL.note: 3,535 cc ('6-cyl. 3535cc/310hp FI'), which rounds to 3.5. KBB's '3.6 Liter' is the nominal figure.

aspiration.note: Fuel-injected DOHC six with no forced induction; inferred.

drivetrain.note: Rear-wheel drive; no opened page states it in words, inferred from the description of the car.

transmission.note: Hagerty: "The same 5-speed manual transmission was utilized throughout production until the final model year in 1995 when the gearbox gained a cog" (the 6-speed came after US sales ended). KBB 1993: 'Transmission Type Manual', '5 speed' (kbb-1993-m5).

powerHp.note: Quote: "The 3.5L 6-cylinder engine now produced 310 hp @ 6,900 rpm and 266 lb-ft. @ 4,750." (BMW NA, under the heading "1991 – 1993 E34 M5"). KBB 1993 Sedan 4D agrees: "Horsepower 310 @ 6900 RPM" (kbb-1993-m5). Same rating for all three US model years per both sources' descriptions.

weightLb.note: PROVISIONAL (database). Sedan, 5-speed manual (the only configuration). Quote (KBB 1993 M5 Sedan 4D): "Curb Weight 3804 lbs." iSeeCars 1991 M5: "Curb Weight | 3804 | lbs" (iseecars-1991-m5); the two databases very likely share one data feed, so they count as one source. BMW NA's history agrees on the number but does not label it curb weight: "This allowed the 3,804 lb. sedan to accelerate to 60 mph in 6.1 seconds" (bmw-us-2019-m5-edition-35). Reference year 1991, the launch year; KBB's figure is for 1993 and iSeeCars' for 1991.

provisionalNote: Weight (3,804 lb) rests on KBB (1993) and iSeeCars (1991), databases that probably share one data feed, so effectively one source; BMW NA's history prints the same 3,804 lb but not labelled as curb weight. A BMW NA press kit or technical data sheet for the 1991-1993 M5, or a major magazine specification panel giving the curb weight, would replace it. Power, years and other fields are not provisional.
